True-up asks the owner before it rewrites an edited suite file only when git tracks the edit, so an edit to a suite file that git does not track is overwritten with no question and no archive copy. The owner never gets to turn the upgrade down, and the edit is gone.

An untracked file's edit is held in no commit. [story:turn-down-a-destructive-true-up](.ok-planner/design/stories/turn-down-a-destructive-true-up.md) promises the owner a way to turn down an upgrade that would rewrite their files.

problem:
True-up looks for a person's edits to the files the suite wrote only in git's diff, which never lists a file git does not track. So true-up overwrites an edited file git does not track with no question to the owner and no archive copy, and the edit is lost.

True-up is the suite's upgrade pass. It rewrites each suite-owned file, one the suite writes and stamps with its version, to the new release's text. Rewriting a file a person edited is destructive. Before a destructive plan runs, the front door, `/ok`, asks the owner once, and true-up copies the file into the archive. [story:turn-down-a-destructive-true-up](.ok-planner/design/stories/turn-down-a-destructive-true-up.md) promises the owner a way to turn down an upgrade that rewrites their files.
